review.translation: [because|0] [in|1] [seven|3] [more|2] [days|1] [I|4] [will cause it to rain|5] [on|6] [the earth|7] {for} [forty|8] [days|9] [and forty|10] [nights|11], [and I will wipe|12] [every|14,13] [living thing|15] [that|16] [I have made|17] [off|18] [the surface of|19] [the ground|20].”

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason for the preceding instructions to Noah. God explains that in seven days he will make it rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לְיָמִים עוֹד שִׁבְעָה, שִׁבְעָה counts the days remaining before the rain begins. The phrase means “in seven more days.”
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ prefixed to a masculine plural absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In לְיָמִים עוֹד שִׁבְעָה, עוֹד marks the seven days remaining before the rain begins. The following forty days and forty nights give the duration of the rain.
analysis.morphology: Temporal adverb without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: yet (so long), within (of time still to run)

analysis.evidence: In לְיָמִים עוֹד שִׁבְעָה, “in seven more days,” שִׁבְעָה counts the masculine plural noun יָמִים and gives the interval before the rain begins.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, masculine singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: In אָנֹכִי מַמְטִיר, the pronoun supplies the subject of the participle מַמְטִיר. Yahweh tells Noah what he himself will do in seven days: “I will cause it to rain.”
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, first person common singular, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אָנֹכִי identifies the speaker as the one who will cause the rain to fall. עַל הָאָרֶץ specifies where it will fall, and the forty days and forty nights specify its duration. The seven-day interval places the action in the future.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil active participle, masculine singular absolute, used predicatively with אָנֹכִי.

analysis.evidence: In מַמְטִיר עַל הָאָרֶץ, עַל introduces the surface on which the rain will fall, הָאָרֶץ (“the earth”).
analysis.morphology: Preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מַמְטִיר עַל הָאָרֶץ, the earth receives the rain. The promise to wipe away כָּל הַיְקוּם אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי, everything God has made that lives on the ground, gives the statement its broad scope.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: אַרְבָּעִים counts יוֹם in אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם, “forty days.” The parallel וְאַרְבָּעִים לָיְלָה, “and forty nights,” completes the duration of the rain.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לָיְלָה, “forty days and forty nights,” אַרְבָּעִים counts the days of rain. The Hebrew noun is singular after “forty.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: In אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לָיְלָה, the marked numeral counts the nights. The conjunction וְ joins “forty nights” to “forty days” to express the duration of the rain.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute, with prefixed conjunction וְ.

analysis.evidence: אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לָיְלָה means “forty days and forty nights.” The repeated numeral counts the nights alongside the days. Both Hebrew nouns are singular.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun in its pausal form.

analysis.evidence: The direct object אֶת כָּל הַיְקוּם אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי identifies what the speaker will wipe out as every living thing he has made. מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה specifies where they will be removed from: the face of the ground.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ introduces a Qal perfect in the first person common singular. This weqatal continues the announcement of what the speaker will do.
analysis.sense: Wipe out living beings from the face of the earth.

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces כָּל הַיְקוּם אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי (“every living thing that I have made”) as the direct object of וּמָחִיתִי (“I will wipe out”).
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in the form אֶת, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת כָּל הַיְקוּם, כָּל quantifies the definite collective noun הַיְקוּם. The whole phrase is the object of וּמָחִיתִי, expressing the full extent of what God will wipe away.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל הַיְקוּם אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי means “every living thing that I have made.” The phrase is the object of וּמָחִיתִי, “I will wipe out,” and מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה locates those living things on the surface of the ground.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying כָּל הַיְקוּם, “every living thing.” Its antecedent supplies the understood object of עָשִׂיתִי, “I made,” yielding “every living thing that I made.”
analysis.morphology: Indeclinable relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל־הַיְקוּם אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי, “every living thing that I made,” the living things are the object of עָשִׂיתִי. The speaker identifies what he will wipe away as what he previously brought into being.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, first person common singular, with subject ending ־תִי.

analysis.evidence: In וּמָחִיתִי … מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, עַל locates what is to be wiped away on the surface of the ground, and מֵ־ marks removal from that surface.
analysis.morphology: Preposition עַל with prefixed מֵ־ (מִן, “from”).

analysis.evidence: In מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “from the surface of the ground,” פְּנֵי is in construct with הָאֲדָמָה and names the surface from which all that lives will be wiped away.
analysis.morphology: Common-gender plural noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “from the face of the ground,” הָאֲדָמָה completes the construct phrase with פְּנֵי. It identifies the surface from which God will wipe away every living thing he has made.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with prefixed definite article הָ־.
analysis.sense: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth
